title: Change Your Circumstances by Changing Your Attitude: The Law of Self-Sabotage
coreMove: Find the constricted attitude that is narrowing your options, then make one expansive action that reveals usable freedom.
sourcePressure: This law is about perception and usable freedom: attitude filters what people notice, attempt, and persist with, so constriction quietly sabotages options.
chapterSpecificMisunderstanding: Turning the law into positive thinking instead of showing how attitude changes perception, action, and opportunity.

hook: a generic "people are not rational" opener for Change Your Circumstances by Changing Your Attitude: The Law of Self-Sabotage
opening with a definition of the law
starting with a vague office conflict
counterintuition: the obvious lesson is wrong because people are complicated

exampleSpecs.domain: a public library branch losing teens and assuming they do not read
exampleSpecs.audience: a librarian whose cynicism is shrinking programming choices
exampleSpecs.stakes: whether the branch loses funding and relevance
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: she replaces the complaint with a test shelf built from teen requests and watches circulation data contradict her assumption
exampleSpecs.firstImage: a rolling book cart with handwritten request slips clipped to the side

exampleSpecs.domain: a small claims defendant convinced the judge will ignore him
exampleSpecs.audience: a legal-aid volunteer pushing against fatalism
exampleSpecs.stakes: whether he forfeits a winnable defense
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: the volunteer has him organize receipts in date order, and the visible stack turns helplessness into one usable argument
exampleSpecs.firstImage: a manila envelope spilling dated receipts onto a courthouse table

exampleSpecs.domain: a refugee language circle where one learner has stopped speaking after mistakes
exampleSpecs.audience: a facilitator seeing shame masquerade as realism
exampleSpecs.stakes: whether practice disappears before fluency can build
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: the facilitator asks him to order tea from a patient vendor once, proving the world did not collapse around an accent
exampleSpecs.firstImage: a paper tea menu creased at the corner of a market stall

exampleSpecs.domain: a theater costume shop after a low-budget production loses its designer
exampleSpecs.audience: a stage manager who assumes scarcity means decline
exampleSpecs.stakes: whether the production becomes smaller or more inventive
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: she predicts disaster, then lays fabric scraps by color and discovers a coherent design language inside the constraint
exampleSpecs.firstImage: bolts of mismatched fabric stacked under a cutting table

exampleSpecs.domain: a neighborhood bike-repair collective facing a broken grant promise
exampleSpecs.audience: a coordinator tempted to call the season dead
exampleSpecs.stakes: whether residents lose access to repairs
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: after the lost grant, he lists donated parts and unused Saturday labor, finding a smaller clinic the old attitude had hidden
exampleSpecs.firstImage: a crate of greasy chains under a tent pole

exampleSpecs.domain: a hotel night auditor applying for a training program after two rejections
exampleSpecs.audience: a worker deciding if rejection proves ceiling or strategy problem
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: she compares the rejected applications, rewrites one skills story, and applies to a smaller certificate instead of declaring the door shut
exampleSpecs.firstImage: a lobby printer glowing beside a stack of application pages

skillTargets: recognize attitude as a perception filter
distinguish expansive action from naive optimism
show how cynicism blocks experiments before reality does

tryThisNowSpec: Name one problem where you have been saying nothing works, then take one small action that assumes one door might still open.

sourceAnchors.name: Anton Chekhov
sourceAnchors.detail: the source uses Chekhov as the anchor for resisting bitterness, educating himself, and widening life through attitude
sourceAnchors.phrasingHint: Chekhov's freedom begins where a constricted attitude would have made his suffering the whole story.
